Local map pack

The real Local Falcon map from the September 28 scan for “dispensary near me,” the strongest shared keyword for both stores. Each pin is a point on the map where we checked Google, and the number is where Beehive Farmacy ranked there. Hover or tap a pin, switch stores, or light up rank groups and distance rings from the panel.

Each scan checks 81 points on a 9x9 grid across a 5-mile radius around the store, so neighboring points are 1.25 miles apart. Distances are measured from the store at the center of the grid, and the distance rings follow the square shape of the grid. “20+” means Beehive Farmacy did not appear in the first 20 Google Maps results at that point. All keywords ranking comparison

Average ranking position

The average position Beehive Farmacy shows up at on Google Maps across every point in the scan grid, when it appears at all. A lower number is better, and 1.00 means first place at every point checked.

Share of local voice

The percentage of the scan grid where Beehive Farmacy shows up in the top 3 map results for that keyword. A higher percentage means more of the surrounding area sees the business at the top of the map pack.

04

What we did this month

Weekly 5-mile radius, 9x9 grid tracking stayed live across all four core keywords at both stores, with scans on September 7, 14, 21 and 28. This report reads the September 28 scan against the August 31 scan, the last scan of each month.

  • Salt Lake City improved on share of local voice, from 26.23% to 35.19% across the four keywords. “Dispensary near me” rose from 48.15% to 71.60% and “dispensary” from 54.32% to 64.20%. Average ranking position moved from 6.60 to 7.22, but only because “pharmacy” (which appears at one or two grid points) read 10.36 on September 28 versus 1.00 on August 31. Average ranking position improved on the other three keywords.
  • Brigham City kept near-total coverage on “dispensary” (96.30%) and “dispensary near me” (93.83%). The pharmacy keywords dipped: “pharmacy near me” fell to 14.81% and “pharmacy” to 30.86% on September 28, after both dropped to 1.23% on September 14. Both returned to 44.44% and 46.91% on the October 5 scan, so we are treating the dips as temporary while we confirm the cause. This is why the Brigham City location average fell from 72.53% to 58.95%.
  • Store-page organic revenue at Salt Lake City was $16,210 against $24,476 in August, while Brigham City held flat at $13,075. Site-wide organic revenue was down only 2.7% ($171,725 against $176,451), so part of the Salt Lake City change is likely visits that began on the homepage rather than on the store page. Tracked profile links (see the action below) will let us confirm this.
  • Link building continued from our authority asset log: 14 assets published between April and August, with 8 confirmed indexed and 6 still indexing, including the five local pages published in August (Brigham City, Box Elder County, Brigham City and Weber County, Salt Lake City, and West Valley 3600 West). Referring domains to beehivefarmacy.com grew from 932 to 1,728 and live backlinks from 3,065 to 5,640 between the September 7 and October 5 snapshots, and domain rating held at 36.
  • Organic keyword visibility needs attention. Ahrefs shows keywords in the top 3 falling from 85 to 74 and total organic keywords from 333 to 261, even as estimated organic traffic rose from 5,791 to 7,195. We will review which terms were lost, as set out in this month's plan.
  • Received domain manager access for trybeehive.com on September 8, which unblocks the tracked redirect for the roadside sign domain, and stayed engaged on the Alpine IQ data integration with Tact Firm and the Beehive team in our weekly working sessions (analytics and progress updates, the RevenueKit and MJ Freeway integration, and the website refresh and patient flow map).
05

This month's plan

  • Apply tracked website links to both Google Business Profiles once approved (see the action below), and complete the tracked redirect for trybeehive.com, so profile visits and roadside sign traffic show up by store in next month's report.
  • Diagnose the Brigham City pharmacy keyword dips on September 14 and 28 by comparing the scan detail and competitor movement for those dates against the stable weeks before them.
  • Audit the organic keywords lost since early September (keywords in the top 3 down from 85 to 74) and fix or refresh the affected pages.
  • Continue testing Google Business Profile category and service-item adjustments at Salt Lake City for “pharmacy” and “pharmacy near me,” both still at 2.47% share of local voice.
  • Confirm indexing on the August local pages and the remaining July listicle, then plan the next batch of link building assets.
06

Next month's plan

  • Re-scan competitors for both stores after the category and relevance changes have had at least two full weekly cycles to take effect.
  • Review Google Business Profile posting and photo cadence at both locations, a lightweight lever we have not leaned on yet this quarter.
  • Report store-level profile traffic and trybeehive.com roadside sign traffic from the new tracked links alongside organic.
  • Trace how much of the growth in referring domains and live backlinks comes from our link building assets, and tie it to ranking movement for each store.
  • Revisit the content and citation plan for Salt Lake City, given the gap between its strong dispensary keywords and its low share of local voice on the pharmacy keywords.
